answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price identities in geography rather than coins. Random verifier nodes, picked each epoch by beacon, ping every key with signed nonces, and the round-trip times build a public atlas of where each key physically runs. Keys whose latency fingerprints match within 2 ms fall into one umber cell, which shares a single reward and vote. So n clones need n machines in distinct network spots, a cost no farm can pool, while an honest agent pays nothing extra. Sparse tundra regions with few verifiers blur the map, so cells there widen and probation runs longer.
